findings.title: Unprotected setOwner() allows arbitrary contract ownership takeover
findings.description: A sensitive state-changing function is externally callable and the signature shows no modifier. It may be protected inside the body — triage will check.
findings.recommendation: Restrict with onlyOwner / role-based access control and emit events for each privileged action.

triage.reason: setOwner is public/external without any access control checks, allowing any user to claim ownership.

findings.title: Reentrancy in withdraw() allows ETH balance drain
findings.description: An external call or token transfer happens before a later state write in the same function, with no nonReentrant guard. A malicious receiver or ERC-777/hook token can re-enter and act on stale state.
findings.recommendation: Apply checks-effects-interactions (update state before the call) and/or OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard.

triage.reason: withdraw() executes an external call to msg.sender before updating balances[msg.sender], allowing recursive calls to drain contract funds.

findings.title: Arbitrary address in transferFrom allows unauthorized deposit execution
findings.description: If `from` is a function argument, anyone can spend tokens from any address that has approved this contract.
findings.recommendation: Pull funds only from msg.sender, or verify a signature/allowance relationship for `from`.

triage.reason: depositUsdcFor allows any caller to transfer USDC from any address 'from' that has granted allowance to the contract.

findings.title: Authorization relying on tx.origin enables phishing attacks
findings.description: tx.origin is the original signer, so any contract the victim interacts with can relay calls that pass this check (phishing-style attack).
findings.recommendation: Authorize with msg.sender (or a signature check) instead of tx.origin.

triage.reason: sweep() relies on tx.origin == owner, enabling phishing attacks via malicious intermediary contracts.

findings.title: Unchecked return value of ERC-20 transferFrom
findings.description: Some tokens (e.g. USDT-style) return false rather than reverting. Ignoring the result lets accounting drift from reality.

triage.reason: The return value of usdc.transferFrom is not checked or wrapped in SafeERC20, which can lead to silent failure for non-reverting ERC20 tokens.

findings.title: Floating pragma
findings.description: Contracts should be deployed with the compiler version they were tested on.

triage.reason: The contract uses floating pragma ^0.8.20 which allows compilation with unverified future compiler versions.

limitations: Judge Sandbox: this is an intentionally vulnerable sample bundled with NightWatch, analyzed by the same pipeline as any real submission.
